literal: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong, Zhang Gun, Deng Yanhai
idiomatic: Volume 21 Biographies 9: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong, Zhang Gun, Deng Yanhai

literal: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong (son Hao), Zhang Gun (younger brother Xun), Deng Yanhai
idiomatic: Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Cui Hong (son Hao), Zhang Gun (younger brother Xun), Deng Yanhai

literal: Yan Feng, style name Zizhang, was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Yan Feng, styled Zizhang, came from Dai.

literal: In youth he loved learning, broadly mastered classics and history, and was skilled in yin-yang lore and prognostic texts.
idiomatic: As a youth he loved study, mastered the classics and histories, and was expert in yin-yang doctrine and prognostic texts.

literal: Zhaocheng had long heard his fame and sent men to summon him with ceremony; Feng did not accept the invitation.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng had long heard of him and sent envoys to summon him with full rites; Feng declined to come.

literal: When the army besieged Dai, he told the townspeople, "If Feng does not come, I shall slaughter you.
idiomatic: When the army besieged Dai, he told the townspeople, "If Feng does not come, I shall slaughter you.

literal: " The people of Dai were afraid and thereupon sent Feng.
idiomatic: The people of Dai were terrified and sent Feng forth.

literal: Zhaocheng received him with guest ceremony.
idiomatic: Zhaocheng received him as an honored guest.

literal: Later he was appointed Left Chief Scribe to the King of Dai and took part in deciding state affairs.
idiomatic: He was later made Left Chief Scribe to the King of Dai and joined in governing the realm.

literal: He also taught the classics to Emperor Xianming.
idiomatic: He also instructed Emperor Xianming in the classics.

literal: Once he was sent on mission to Fu Jian; Jian asked Feng, "What sort of man is the King of Dai?
idiomatic: He was once sent to Fu Jian, who asked Feng, "What manner of man is the King of Dai?

literal: " He replied, "Broad, harmonious, and humane, with far-reaching strategy—a warlord of his age.
idiomatic: Feng answered, "Magnanimous and humane, with far-reaching strategy—the preeminent warlord of the day.

literal: He constantly harbors the will to swallow the realm under heaven.
idiomatic: He constantly aims to unite the realm.

literal: " Jian said, "You northerners have no stout armor or sharp weapons; when the foe is weak you advance, when strong you retreat—how can you annex and absorb them?
idiomatic: Jian said, "You northerners lack stout armor and keen blades; when enemies are weak you advance, when strong you withdraw—how could you conquer and absorb them?

literal: " Feng said, "Northerners are stalwart and fierce; mounted, each carries three weapons and gallops like flight.
idiomatic: Feng said, "Northerners are hardy and fierce; on horseback each man bears three weapons and rides like the wind.

literal: Our lord is heroic and outstanding, rules the northern lands, commands a million bowmen, and his orders are as one.
idiomatic: Our lord is heroic, has won the north, commands a million archers, and his orders are obeyed as one.

literal: The army suffers none of the hardship of baggage trains or camp cooking; it marches light and swift and takes supplies from the enemy.
idiomatic: His armies know none of the drag of supply trains or camp kitchens; they march light and fast and live off the foe.

literal: This is why the south grows weary and broken while the north is ever victorious.
idiomatic: That is why the south wears itself down while the north wins again and again.

literal: " Jian said, "How many men and horses does that state have?
idiomatic: Jian asked, "How many men and horses does that state have?

literal: " Feng said, "Bowmen number in the hundreds of thousands; horses in pasture exceed a million.
idiomatic: Feng said, "Archers number in the hundreds of thousands; grazing horses exceed a million.

literal: " Jian said, "What you say of men may stand, but you speak too many horses.
idiomatic: Jian said, "Your count of men may stand, but your horses are too many.

literal: " Feng said, "From East Mountain to West River along the Yunzhong valley is two hundred li; from North Mountain to South Mountain over a hundred li—every year in mid-autumn horses gather in great numbers and nearly fill the river valley.
idiomatic: Feng said, "From East Mountain to West River along the Yunzhong stretch is two hundred li; from North Mountain to South Mountain is over a hundred li. Each year in mid-autumn the horses gather until the valley is nearly full.

literal: By this reckoning, even what men say does not tell the whole.
idiomatic: By that measure, even what people say falls short of the truth.

literal: When Feng returned, Jian richly rewarded him with gifts.
idiomatic: When Feng returned, Jian sent him lavish gifts.

literal: Xu Qian, style name Yuansun, was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Xu Qian, styled Yuansun, came from Dai.

literal: In youth he had literary talent and was skilled in astronomy, charts, and prognostic learning.
idiomatic: In youth he showed literary talent and mastered astronomy, charts, and prognostic lore.

literal: At the founding of the state his family came over in submission; Zhaocheng promoted him to Palace Gentleman to the King of Dai and put him in charge of written records.
idiomatic: When the state was founded his family submitted; Zhaocheng made him Palace Gentleman to the King of Dai and put him in charge of documents.

literal: Together with Yan Feng he taught the classics to Emperor Xianming.
idiomatic: He and Yan Feng together instructed Emperor Xianming in the classics.

literal: After Zhaocheng died, Qian moved to Chang'an.
idiomatic: After Zhaocheng's death, Qian went to Chang'an.

literal: Fu Jian's younger cousin, the Duke of Xingtang, Luo, held Helong and invited Qian to his commandery.
idiomatic: Fu Jian's younger cousin, the Duke of Xingtang, Luo, governed Helong and asked Qian to join him there.

literal: Before long, because his stepmother was old, he begged leave to return.
idiomatic: Soon, with his stepmother aged, he asked to return home.

literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he returned to Daowu and was made Right Marshal, joining Zhang Gun and others in founding the new order.
idiomatic: At the opening of Dengguo he returned to Daowu, who made him Right Marshal to help Zhang Gun and others lay the foundations of rule.

literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Daowu sent Qian to report the crisis to Yao Xing.
idiomatic: When Murong Bao invaded, Daowu sent Qian to seek aid from Yao Xing.

literal: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong in relief.
idiomatic: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong to rescue them.

literal: Fosong was slow and dilatory; Daowu ordered Qian to write and send him a letter, and Fosong then marched day and night.
idiomatic: Fosong dragged his feet; Daowu had Qian write to him, and Fosong then pressed forward at double speed.

literal: Daowu was greatly pleased and enfeoffed Qian as Marquis Within the Passes.
idiomatic: Daowu was delighted and enfeoffed Qian as Marquis Within the Passes.

literal: When Bao was defeated, Fosong returned.
idiomatic: After Bao's defeat, Fosong withdrew.

literal: When Murong Chui died, Qian submitted a memorial urging accession to the throne.
idiomatic: When Murong Chui died, Qian memorialized urging Daowu to take the imperial title.

literal: When Bing Province was pacified, Qian was made Protector of Yangqu and enfeoffed Marquis of Pingshu.
idiomatic: After Bing Province was pacified, Qian became Protector of Yangqu and Marquis of Pingshu.

literal: On his death he was posthumously made Governor of You Province and Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Wen.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Governor of You Province and Duke of Gaoyang, with the posthumous name Wen.

literal: His son Luoyang inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Luoyang succeeded to the title.

literal: Mingyuan later recorded Qian's service and made Luoyang Governor of Yanmen.
idiomatic: Mingyuan later honored Qian's service and appointed Luoyang Governor of Yanmen.

literal: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of fine grain grew, each with different furrows but a single ear.
idiomatic: On Luoyang's family fields three stalks of fine grain grew, each from a different furrow yet bearing one ear.

literal: Taiwu was pleased and advanced his rank to Duke of Beidi.
idiomatic: Taiwu was pleased and raised him to Duke of Beidi.

literal: On his death his posthumous name was Gong.
idiomatic: At his death his posthumous name was Gong.

literal: Cui Hong, style name Xuanbo, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, sixth-generation descendant of Wei Minister of Works Cui Lin.
idiomatic: Cui Hong, styled Xuanbo, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe, sixth in descent from Cui Lin, Minister of Works of Wei.

literal: His grandfather Yue served Shi Jilong as Right Chief Scribe to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yue served Shi Jilong as Right Chief Scribe to the Minister of Works.

literal: His father Qian served Murong Yong as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: His father Qian served Murong Yong as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

literal: Both were famed for talent and learning.
idiomatic: Both were renowned for learning and ability.

literal: Hong in youth had outstanding talent and was called the divine child of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Hong as a youth showed exceptional talent and was called the prodigy of Ji Province.

literal: When Fu Rong governed Ji Province he received him with humble courtesy.
idiomatic: When Fu Rong governed Ji Province he treated Hong with humble respect.

literal: He was appointed Gentleman to the Duke of Yangping and Concurrent Administrator of Ji Province retainers.
idiomatic: He was made Gentleman to the Duke of Yangping and Concurrent Administrator of Ji Province staff.

literal: Going out he oversaw all affairs; coming in he was a guest and companion—all business was put in order and decisions never stalled.
idiomatic: Abroad he managed affairs; at court he was counselor and friend—every task was set in order and nothing hung unresolved.

literal: Fu Jian heard of him and summoned him as Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: Fu Jian heard of him and summoned him as Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

literal: He declined on grounds of his mother's illness and did not go.
idiomatic: He pleaded his mother's illness and declined.

literal: He was demoted to Assistant in the Office for Compilation.
idiomatic: He was demoted to Assistant in the Office for Compilation.

literal: Hao Xuan of Taiyuan, famed for knowing men, said Hong had the talent of a chief minister—unmatched in recent generations.
idiomatic: Hao Xuan of Taiyuan, famed for judging men, said Hong had the makings of a chief minister, unmatched in his generation.

literal: When Jian fell, Hong took refuge between Qi and Lu and was detained by the Dingling Zhai Zhao and the Jin rebel general Zhang Yuan.
idiomatic: When Jian's state collapsed, Hong fled to Qi and Lu and was held by the Dingling leader Zhai Zhao and the Jin rebel Zhang Yuan.

literal: Hao Xuan sighed, "Such a man, in such a time—without the wind beneath a soaring ascent, he sinks and flies with sparrows; how regrettable!"
idiomatic: Hao Xuan sighed, "A man like this, in a time like this—without the updraft of fortune he sinks to fly with sparrows. What a waste!"

literal: He served Murong Chui as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, and Internal Governor of Gaoyang—every post won praise.
idiomatic: He served Murong Chui as Director of Personnel, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, and Internal Governor of Gaoyang, winning praise in every office.

literal: Upright in conduct, even amid war he alone kept his will and pursued learning zealously, caring nothing for property; wife and children did not escape hunger and cold.
idiomatic: Upright in character, even in war he held to study and took no thought for wealth; his wife and children knew hunger and cold.

literal: When Daowu campaigned against Murong Bao he halted at Zhongshan.
idiomatic: When Daowu marched against Murong Bao he camped at Zhongshan.

literal: Hong abandoned his commandery and fled to the seacoast.
idiomatic: Hong abandoned his commandery and fled toward the sea.

literal: The emperor had long heard his name and sent men to seek him.
idiomatic: The emperor had long heard of him and sent men to find him.

literal: When he arrived he was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and, with Zhang Gun, jointly managed the keys of state and drafted institutions anew.
idiomatic: On his arrival he was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; with Zhang Gun he shared control of state affairs and drafted new institutions.

literal: At that time Jin envoys came on a friendly mission; the emperor wished to respond and ordered the relevant offices to deliberate the state name.
idiomatic: Jin envoys then came on a friendly mission; the emperor wished to reply and ordered deliberation on the dynastic name.

literal: Hong argued, "The titles of the Three August Ones and Five Emperors were sometimes taken from the land where they arose, sometimes from the name of the state they enfeoffed.
idiomatic: Hong argued, "The Three August Ones and Five Emperors took their titles either from the soil that bore them or from the states they were enfeoffed to rule.

literal: Thus Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou at first were all feudal lords; when sagely virtue rose high, the myriad states honored them, and their titles followed their origins without change.
idiomatic: Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou began as feudal lords; when their virtue towered, all realms acclaimed them and their titles kept to their roots without change.

literal: Only the Shang people moved repeatedly and changed their title to Yin.
idiomatic: Only the Shang moved their seat again and again and changed their name to Yin.

literal: Yet both names were still used and the title of the founding base was not cast off.
idiomatic: Yet both names were used together and the founding title was never abandoned.

literal: Thus the Odes say 'the host of Yin and Shang'—this is the meaning.
idiomatic: Hence the Odes speak of 'the host of Yin and Shang'—that is the sense.

literal: Though our state now rules the broad northern wastes, down to Your Majesty it has answered the times and risen like a dragon in flight.
idiomatic: Though our state rules the vast northern wastes, under Your Majesty it has answered Heaven and risen like a dragon.

literal: Though called an old domain, its mandate is wholly new.
idiomatic: Though called an old domain, its mandate is wholly new.

literal: Therefore at the beginning of Dengguo Dai was changed to Wei.
idiomatic: Therefore at the opening of Dengguo Dai was renamed Wei.

literal: Murong Yong also presented the territory of Wei.
idiomatic: Murong Yong likewise offered up the lands of Wei.

literal: Wei is the great name of a state above the provinces—this is the proof of revolution and the dark sign of favorable seeing.
idiomatic: Wei is the great name of a state above the commanderies—the sign of revolution and the omen of Heaven's favor.

literal: Your servant is foolish and thinks the title should be Wei.
idiomatic: This humble servant believes the dynastic name should be Wei.

literal: " Daowu followed this, and thereafter they were called Wei.
idiomatic: Daowu agreed, and from then on they were called Wei.

literal: When the emperor visited Ye he questioned him repeatedly on precedent.
idiomatic: When the emperor visited Ye he questioned Hong at length on precedent.

literal: Hong answered as if flowing; the emperor was pleased.
idiomatic: Hong answered fluently and won the emperor's approval.

literal: Returning he halted at Mount Heng; the emperor in person climbed the summit to comfort the newly relocated people and happened upon Hong supporting his aged mother up the ridge; he granted them oxen and grain.
idiomatic: On the return he stopped at Mount Heng; the emperor climbed the summit to comfort new settlers and found Hong helping his old mother up the path—he gave them oxen and grain.

literal: He then ordered that migrants unable to go on their own be given carts and oxen.
idiomatic: He then ordered carts and oxen for migrants who could not travel on foot.

literal: Hong was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
idiomatic: Hong was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

literal: When orders went out to fix ranks and titles, draft court ritual, harmonize music, establish laws and statutes, and enforce prohibitions, Hong oversaw and trimmed all of it as lasting model.
idiomatic: When the court set ranks and titles, drafted ritual, harmonized music, fixed laws, and enforced prohibitions, Hong directed and shaped them into lasting forms.

literal: When the Eight Departments grandees were established to mirror the Eight Dignitaries,
idiomatic: When the Eight Department grandees were created on the model of the Eight Dignitaries,

literal: Hong broadly supervised the thirty-six bureaus like ministers and vice-ministers directing affairs.
idiomatic: Hong broadly supervised the thirty-six bureaus as ministers and vice-ministers direct government.

literal: Deeply trusted, his power tilted the court.
idiomatic: Deeply trusted, his influence dominated the court.

literal: Frugal in his own living, he built no estates; his house had nothing but four bare walls;
idiomatic: He lived frugally and amassed no property; his home was bare to the four walls;

literal: going out he had no carriage and morning and evening he walked to court.
idiomatic: abroad he had no carriage and walked to court morning and evening.

literal: His mother was seventy; he could not supply her with rich fare.
idiomatic: His mother was seventy and he could not give her lavish meals.

literal: When the emperor heard, he esteemed him all the more and sent rich gifts.
idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he esteemed him further and sent generous gifts.

literal: Some in the age also mocked his excessive frugality, yet Hong lived all the more strictly.
idiomatic: Some mocked his austerity, yet Hong lived more strictly still.

literal: He was often summoned to ask about old affairs of past ages and the institutions of kings; Hong set forth the forms of ancient making and the causes of rise and fall in former dynasties, greatly matching the emperor's intent.
idiomatic: He was often called to discuss antiquity and royal institutions; Hong explained ancient forms and the causes of dynastic rise and fall, greatly pleasing the emperor.

literal: He never spoke bluntly against the will, nor flattered to win favor.
idiomatic: He never spoke bluntly to offend, nor flattered for favor.

literal: In Daowu's last years many great ministers provoked imperial wrath, yet Hong alone was never punished—because of this.
idiomatic: In Daowu's last years many ministers drew imperial wrath, yet Hong alone was never rebuked—for this reason.

literal: The emperor once summoned Hong to discuss the Book of Han; when they came to Lou Jing urging the Han founder to marry the Princess of Lu to the Xiongnu, he was pleased and sighed long.
idiomatic: The emperor once had Hong discuss the Book of Han; at Lou Jing's counsel to marry the Princess of Lu to the Xiongnu he was pleased and sighed long.

literal: Therefore all imperial princesses were married to tributary states; sons of court ministers and fine clans could not marry them.
idiomatic: Hence all imperial princesses were married to tributary states, and courtiers' sons and eminent families could not wed them.

literal: When the Secretariat post was abolished, Hong was enfeoffed Marquis of Baima and made General of Zhoubing.
idiomatic: When the Secretariat was abolished, Hong was enfeoffed Marquis of Baima and made General of Zhoubing.

literal: He shared rank with old meritocrats Yu Yue and Xi Jin, yet favor and trust passed beyond them.
idiomatic: He stood in the same rank as veterans Yu Yue and Xi Jin, yet enjoyed greater favor.

literal: When Daowu died, Mingyuan had not yet taken the throne; the Prince of Qinghe, Shao, because hearts were unsettled, distributed great wealth and silks, bestowing gifts on court gentlemen.
idiomatic: When Daowu died, before Mingyuan had taken the throne, Prince Shao of Qinghe, seeing unrest in men's hearts, lavished wealth and silks on the court.
